hints: Look carefully at the whole circle in the photomicrograph at x60. Notice the very thick wall compared to the central lumen and the wavy inner edge, what mammalian tube looks like this in transverse section?
Remember the three layers of that tube from inside to outside: endothelium lining, then a thick middle layer, then an outer layer. Which layer is W pointing to in the middle of the wall?
walkthrough:
**Identify the structure**

Great first step is to name what you are looking at. You see a circular tube cut in transverse section with a thick wall and a relatively small, round lumen.

The inner edge looks slightly folded. That is classic for an artery, not a vein or capillary.

**Recall the three tunics of an artery**

Now recall the plan from inside to outside. The innermost tunica intima is a thin endothelium of squamous cells plus a little connective tissue.

Next is the thick tunica media. Then the outer tunica externa (adventitia).

**Locate layer W and conclude**

The label line for W points to the thick middle band of the wall, not the very thin lining next to the lumen and not the loose outer coat.

That middle band is the tunica media, whose main components are smooth muscle to allow vasoconstriction and elastic fibres to allow stretch and recoil. So C is the match.

options.A: Collagen fibres only describes part of the outer tunica externa, not the thick muscular middle layer W.
options.B: Elastic fibres plus collagen fibres without muscle is also a description of the outer layer, so it does not fit the thick middle layer W.
options.C: W is the tunica media of the artery, which is mainly smooth muscle with elastic fibres for contraction and elastic recoil.
options.D: Squamous endothelium is the very thin tunica intima lining the lumen, not the thick layer W further out in the wall.
